flashcards.back: The distance covered in one unit of time: a speed of 60 km/h means the bus covers 60 km in every hour.
An amount per unit of something else: speed is a rate, the distance travelled per hour.
How far something travels, found by multiplying speed by time: at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours the distance is 150 km.
How long a journey lasts: the time together with the speed decides the distance, so half an hour gives half the distance of a full hour.

A rate is read as a total instead of an amount per unit of time. Speed is distance per hour: after half an hour at 60 km/h the bus has gone 30 km, not 60. In the animation scene s3 the claim is tested against the road and fails: after half an hour the bus sits at the 30 km mark, not the 60 km mark.
